# TODO / site notes

Working notes for `cocokane.github.io`. The site is a static Claude Design export —
`index.html` is the bundled page that actually gets served.

---

## Read this first: hand-edits vs. re-export

`index.html`, `_export_src.html` and the two `Academic Site*.dc.html` canvases are all
**generated by Claude Design**. Everything below was hand-patched into those files.

- A change must be applied to **all** of them, or the next export silently reverts it.
- **Re-exporting from Claude Design will overwrite these hand-edits entirely** — the design
  tool has no knowledge of them. After any re-export, re-apply anything you want to keep.
- In `index.html` the markup lives inside a JS string literal where `"` is written `\"`
  and `/` is written `/`. String surgery there must account for that. (A find on
  `</div>` will *not* match; it appears as `</div>`.)
- Verify any edit by rendering, not by eye:
  ```
  "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" \
    --headless --dump-dom --virtual-time-budget=20000 "file://$PWD/index.html"
  ```
  Sanity check: `index.html` should contain exactly **2** `<!DOCTYPE` (the bundle embeds a
  second one). Three means the file got duplicated by a bad patch.

  34–66% band keeps the text column at exactly the original `#23262b`; only the outer

- **Sidequests hover dropout** — the menu sits `margin-top:14px` below its button, and that
  gap belonged to neither element, so the wrapper's `onMouseLeave` fired as the pointer

- **Publications** now sync from ORCID. They previously queried
  `api.openalex.org/works?filter=author.orcid:<id>`, which returns **0 results** — no
  OpenAlex author record carries that ORCID. OpenAlex picks ORCIDs up from publisher
  Crossref deposits, *not* from ORCID profile edits, so editing ORCID could never have
  fixed it. Now: fetch `pub.orcid.org/v3.0/<orcid>/works`, collect DOIs, batch-resolve them
  against OpenAlex (`filter=doi:a|b|c`) for author lists and venue names. Adding a work on
  ORCID is enough — no code change needed.
- Background wave grid made denser: dots `(0.10 + 0.32·v)` → `(0.17 + 0.50·v)`,
  connecting lines `a * 0.35` → `a * 0.46`.
- Quora link pointed at the generic homepage; now goes to the profile and reads
  "Quora (when it used to be good)". Sidequests dropdown widened 300px → 404px so that
  label sits on one line next to Instagram.
- **Profile photo re-cropped from the original.** The embedded photo was only 252×336, so
  zooming it with a CSS `transform:scale()` upscaled ~2× and looked blurry. Now the crop is
  baked in at full resolution instead: source
  `/Users/yashkokane/Documents/Kundli/Photos/Yash_Semiformal.jpeg` (4284×5712), cropped to
  box `(882, 1844, 3402, 4957)` — 2520×3113, matching the 170:210 frame aspect — and
  resized to **510×630 WebP** (3× the 170×210 display size, so it is never upscaled).
  No CSS transform on the `<img>` any more. Embedded as a base64 data URI in `index.html`,
  `_export_src.html` **and** `.image-slots.state.json` (the design tool's own copy — keep
  the three in sync). The `.dc.html` canvases use an image-slot placeholder and have no
  photo to update.
  To re-frame: pick a new crop box on the original at 0.8095 aspect and re-encode. Headroom
  is just the top edge of the box.

**Mobile layout** (≤760px). The page is all inline styles with no classes, so the
responsive rules live in one `@media (max-width: 760px)` block in the helmet `<style>` and
hook elements with **attribute-substring selectors** on the `style` attribute, e.g.
`div[style*='grid-template-columns: 180px']`. Every rule needs `!important` to beat the
inline value. Two gotchas:
- The rendered DOM serialises inline styles *with* spaces (`grid-template-columns: 180px`)
  while the source has none, so each selector lists both forms.
- Headless Chrome clamps every mode to a 500px minimum viewport, so `--window-size=390`
  silently tests at 500. To test a real phone width, load the page inside a 390px
  `<iframe>` (with `--allow-file-access-from-files` to read results back out).
What the block does: nav wraps and centres (height auto); `main` top padding raised to
128px to clear the taller nav; header stacks (`flex-direction: column`); h1 42→34px,
h2 28→24px; justified paragraphs go left-aligned (rivers at narrow measure); the 180px and
110px label columns collapse to one column; the Sidequests menu re-parents to the nav
(`position: static` on its wrapper) and anchors `left:14px; right:14px` so it can never
leave the viewport.

**Analytics — GoatCounter** (site code `cocokane`, dashboard at
https://cocokane.goatcounter.com). One tag, last thing in the page template body:
`<script data-goatcounter="https://cocokane.goatcounter.com/count" async src="https://gc.zgo.at/count.js">`.
Why *there*: the bundled `index.html` parses its template with `DOMParser`, swaps it in with
`replaceWith`, then re-creates every `<script>` (copying attributes) and awaits each `src`
script's `onload`/`onerror` **in document order**. A tag in the outer shell `<head>` would be
discarded by the swap; a tag placed before the component script would delay the app until
count.js loaded. Placed last, it can't block anything, and an adblocker just resolves
through `onerror`. It lives in `index.html` and `_export_src.html` only — not the
`.dc.html` canvases, which would count design-tool views as visits. count.js does not
count `localhost`/`file://` by default, so local previews stay out of the numbers. It shows
aggregate visits, referrers and countries — never individual identities.

## Hidden — quantum-mechanics background glyphs

Seven minimal gold (`#e0b46a`) inline-SVG glyphs: Gaussian wave packet, EM wave,
p-orbital, harmonic oscillator with energy levels, double-slit interference, Bloch sphere,
particle in a box. Randomly scattered and rotated (−27°..+27°), each on a slow independent
drift. Anchored outside the 680px text column via `calc(50% + 340px + Npx)`, verified not
to overlap `main`.

**Currently hidden.** The layer is intact, just switched off.

- **To re-enable:** delete `display:none;` from the layer's style
  (`position:fixed; inset:0; overflow:hidden; pointer-events:none; z-index:0; display:none;`)
  in `index.html`, `_export_src.html` and `Academic Site v2.dc.html`.
- Rotation rides in a CSS variable (`--rot`) because the drift animation already owns
  `transform`; the keyframes compose them as `rotate(var(--rot)) translateY(...)`.
  A plain `transform: rotate()` on the element would be overwritten by the animation.
- The arrangement is a fixed seeded scatter, not re-rolled per page load — a per-load roll
  can cluster glyphs or drop one behind the nav.
